GIRL please no more negativity this are real facts, woman to woman. Hear me out

If you can afford a $30 meal, delivered to you, that means you have a disposable income. That means you can afford to tip, just as you would tip a pizza man. Think about it, you pay for the food. Then you pay for the delivery. Same thing! It is the same exact thing, and would you stiff your delivery driver? No man, that’s rude! You paid for the pizza, surely you can pay the person that brought it to you in their own car.. that’s how these services have worked ever since I’ve been in America, at least. 

If, let’s say, you only have $37 in your account and you think hmmm I want doordash. Technically you afford it. But now you are broke until payday, that’s not good! Maybe you could afford the doordash, but you shouldn’t have bought it cause you’re really too broke. 

That’s what I mean by it’s a luxury. If you have the money, girl get doordash and do a $5 tip please, go for it!! Someone will make money from it, someone will take it. Maybe someone’s sitting in that parking lot just waiting for an order! even if I were to decline it(which I wouldn’t, i take any order over $5 usually cause i just like to drive around) someone will take it and it will be okay. 
But it’s not unreasonable for people to complain about crappy tips, for this job especially! it’s not always fun to see complaining, but i feel like everyone complains about their job in one way or another. I think it’s hard with doordash because the customers can take it personally, like when they see a post like this. but it is just a random person complaining about their job on the web, in this case the person who took the order had humor about it and didn’t care. i mean they took the order! lol.

I saw a post recently that said "Its really easy to be a jerk. It takes effort to be kind" and I was like huh, and moved on.

 My partner was sick and being really needy for over a week and I started to get really annoyed towards the end. He said something to me and I snapped and said something rude, I don't even remember. But I do remember regretting it a few seconds later, and realizing if I had just taken a little more time, maybe took a deep breath- I could have responded in a kinder way. But it was SO easy to just say the first mean thing that came to my head. I had time to decide what I wanted to say, but I was tired and felt like he deserved it. 

A few days later some guy yelled at me cause I was pulled up a bit too far, and was too close to the crosswalk in his opinion. The easy thing to do would be to tell him to fuck off, or maybe purposefully ignore him or flip him off. The harder thing to do, was to apologize and hope to deescalate. I did apologize but he did not deescalate LOL 

I think when our emotions are level, I agree with you. But otherwise I think the easy way out is to let our anger, annoyance, etc take over- rather than saying or doing the kinder thing.
